title: Living it close
hook: Jacob sleeps on a roadside stone and wakes: surely the LORD is in this place, and I knew it not
tomorrow: who was still beside him at the top of the mountain?

segments.voice: At the end of the Gita, Krishna said: reflect, then do as you choose. An invitation, the choice left free. Today this whole stretch of living it comes to a close.

The last day of something, a job, a season, a routine, and it turns out to be an ordinary Thursday. Nobody makes a speech. In Genesis, Jacob is on the run from his brother, alone. The sun sets on a plain stretch of road. He takes one of the stones of that place for a pillow and lies down. He dreams of a ladder set on the earth, its top reaching to heaven, angels going up and down on it, and God standing above it with a promise. Then he wakes up, on the same hard ground.
screen: `AN ORDINARY LAST THURSDAY.` → `A STONE FOR A PILLOW.` → `A LADDER, AND ANGELS.` → `HE WAKES ON THE SAME GROUND.`

segments.voice: And he says: "Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not." Then: "this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven." Notice what place he means. Not a temple. A roadside, with a rock for a pillow. In the morning he sets that stone up as a pillar, pours oil on it, and names the spot Beth-el, house of God. The rabbis of the Talmud found one more thing in this night. Genesis says Jacob lighted upon a certain place, and they read that as prayer, and credit Jacob with the evening prayer, maariv. So the man on the run, sleeping rough, becomes the father of praying at night. That is the teaching Genesis hands down: God can be met in a place that looks like nothing, and the ordinary ground can turn out to be the gate. And that's what living it close means. Not waiting for the big moment. The plain pickup, the evening review, the spice box, the one breath: this was it, the whole time.
screen: `SURELY THE LORD IS IN THIS PLACE.` · `NOT A TEMPLE: A ROADSIDE.` · `BETH-EL, HOUSE OF GOD.` · `JACOB AND THE EVENING PRAYER.` · then, large: `THIS IS IT.`

segments.voice: Let yourself lean back and rest, as if the ground beneath you were enough. When you're settled, lift your eyes: to the ceiling, the window, the sky. Stay with whatever is right there above you until the bell.
Living it close: practice brought home to plain days and places, the way Jacob found the gate of heaven by the road.
Your line: this is it, the roadside and the stone, and I knew it not. Living it, done.
